faq.q: Is it okay to feel angry?
faq.a: Yes. Anger is a normal feeling, and it often tells you something seems unfair. Feeling angry is fine; hurting people or things is not.
asks: Am I bad if I get angry?

faq.q: What should I do if I am about to explode?
faq.a: Stop and step away if you can. Take five slow breaths, count to ten, or squeeze something soft. Talk about it once you feel calmer.
asks: What do I do when I am really furious?

faq.q: Why does breathing help when I am angry?
faq.a: Slow breaths slow your heart and tell your brain's alarm that you are safe. Then the thinking part of your brain can switch back on.
asks: Does taking deep breaths really work?

faq.q: How can I say I am angry without shouting?
faq.a: Try "I feel angry when you take my things. Please ask first." Saying the feeling and what you need works much better than shouting.
asks: How do I tell someone I am cross?

faq.q: Why do I get angry so quickly sometimes?
faq.a: Being tired, hungry or worried makes the anger bottle easier to shake. A snack, some rest or talking about what is bothering you can help.
asks: Why am I so grumpy today?

facts: The word "hangry", hungry plus angry, was added to the Oxford English Dictionary in 2018.
Anger usually builds in stages, so noticing early signs like a hot face or tight fists gives you time to calm down.
